topic: Frugal Tokens: Explore Cost and Usage Across All Your Coding Agents

key_points: Show HN (37 pts) — local, read-only view of token usage and reported cost across OpenCode, Claude Code, PI, Codex, and Cursor sessions
Runs locally in Deno (2.9+), read-only, never mutates agent databases; open at localhost:9000
Per-session explorer is the standout feature; surfaces cache misses, TTL misses, and their monetary cost
Cross-harness comparison shows token usage differences across tools (Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku tiering themes)
Independently verified data points matter for companies/individuals measuring ROI on token spend
Local-first desktop and web app for browsing/searching/analyzing past AI coding sessions
Auto-discovers and reads session data from dozens of agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Qwen, DeepSeek, etc.)
Token Usage & Cost reports, cached vs uncached breakdown, session intelligence, activity/recent-edits views
Backed by a SQLite/Postgres/DuckDB sync backend with reporting and export
Coding-agent spend tracker; HN user noted it 'only tells you spend not messages and everything else'
Focused purely on dollar spend rather than granular token/message/cache diagnostics
Positioned as a simpler spend-only alternative for teams that just want the bottom line
Free, local-first observability for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and 4 more providers
Tracks subagent behavior and cost; zero config, zero cloud dependency; brew install
Team-wide cost management, agent config scanner, cost calculator, 2026 Cost Report PDF with industry data
Offers free/Pro/Team/Enterprise tiers with a 'cut AI costs 40%' email course
Show HN tool for token and cost tracking across AI coding agents
Lightweight metric-focused approach compared to fuller observability suites
Part of the emerging 'agentic metrics' category alongside Frugal Tokens, BurnRate, AgentsView

stats.fact: A single TTL cache miss (responding ~1.5 hours later) cost $6 for one message in a Fable session, per an HN user on the Frugal Tokens thread.
Many users have 'no idea how many cache misses were happening' after stepping away for an hour or more — idle gaps invalidate prompt caches and inflate cost.
Frugal Tokens tracks token usage and reported cost for at least 5 harnesses: OpenCode, Claude Code, PI (Apple), Codex, and Cursor.
AgentsView reads session data from dozens of AI coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Qwen, DeepSeek, OpenCode and more.
Frugal Tokens performs cache-miss pricing analysis (uncachedInput, cacheRead, cacheWrite 5m/1h) to estimate the extra cost of broken cache reuse.
Independent, cross-harness token-usage data is 'super important for companies measuring ROI on token spend as they recover from letting people go wild on token usage in the past year.'

angles: The hidden cost of prompt-cache misses — stepping away for an hour can make the next turn bill as uncached input; TTL misses can cost dollars per single message.
Cross-harness token usage comparison — the same task burns different tokens in OpenCode vs Claude Code vs Codex vs Cursor; independent verification beats vendor claims.
Local-first / read-only privacy angle — no code ever leaves the machine, no cloud dependency, so it's safe for teams with sensitive codebases.
ROI governance angle — as companies tighten budgets after a year of unchecked agent spend, per-session cost diagnostics become a governance requirement, not a nicety.
Cache-frugality as a workflow lever — understanding cacheWrite/cacheRead and session shape lets developers redesign prompts/tooling to cut recurring cost.
